nodes.label: Evo Cognitive OS
nodes.description: A local-first cognitive operating system that helps people continue work instead of reconstructing it.

nodes.label: Evo Architecture
nodes.description: Consists of Constitution, Cognitive Model, Architectural Laws, Behavioral Trace, and RFC-0000 through RFC-0009.

nodes.label: Gstack Integration
nodes.description: Integration with gstack skills including browser automation and review tools.

nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph
nodes.description: Knowledge graph maintenance and query rules for repository navigation.

nodes.label: Cognitive Continuity Layer
nodes.description: The foundational computing primitive that preserves work continuity across applications and time.

nodes.label: Local-First Architecture
nodes.description: Privacy-first architecture ensuring user data stays local, serving as a trust moat.

nodes.label: Work Restoration Wedge
nodes.description: The initial wedge getting users back into projects exactly where they left off without reconstruction.

nodes.label: Evidence Reconciliation
nodes.description: Adversarial re-verification of research claims, invalidating unsupported statistics and framing.

nodes.label: Pre-Seed Pitch Deck
nodes.description: A 10-12 slide investor deck grounded in research and constrained by hard prohibitions.

nodes.label: Graphify Pipeline
nodes.description: Pipeline transforming files into an interactive knowledge graph with GraphRAG JSON and reports.

nodes.label: Evo System
nodes.description: Local-first system that maintains immutable observation log and derives work understanding for restoration.

nodes.label: Observation
nodes.description: Canonical, append-only record of what Evo witnessed - forms the foundational data layer.

nodes.label: Evidence
nodes.description: Facts that a witnessed record establishes - canonical derived facts from observations.

nodes.label: Artifact
nodes.description: A thing with a history - canonical identity representing files, URLs, repositories, documents.

nodes.label: Workspace
nodes.description: Projection representing ongoing body of work - derived from engagements, no longer persisted.

nodes.label: Engagement
nodes.description: New architectural level between observations and workspace that was previously missing.

nodes.label: Work Restoration
nodes.description: Core purpose of Evo - put person back into state when they stopped, in seconds, so resuming never costs more attention than the work itself.

nodes.label: Local-First Principle
nodes.description: Architectural constraint - no component requires network call to function.

nodes.label: Immutable Observation Log
nodes.description: The observation log is immutable and append-only, forever - forms the foundation of the system.

nodes.label: Derived Views Principle
nodes.description: Everything except observation log, artifact identity, knowledge, and decisions is derived and disposable.

nodes.label: Selective Restoration
nodes.description: Restoration opens the minimum that re-establishes work and preserves access to the rest.

nodes.label: Work Identity
nodes.description: Formed from overlapping, non-transitive nuclei and propagated as stable WorkId through projections.

nodes.label: Nuclei Clustering
nodes.description: New approach using overlapping nuclei instead of resource/context partition for work formation.

nodes.label: Standing
nodes.description: Classification system for work threads - Primary, Continuation, Continuable, or HistoryOnly.

nodes.label: Specificity
nodes.description: Measure that gates titling and resume-point eligibility - prevents over-broad naming.

nodes.label: Workspace Formation
nodes.description: Process that creates coherent bodies of work from artifacts - currently lacks multi-artifact formation signals.

nodes.label: Proliferation Failure
nodes.description: System creates too many single-artifact workspaces - 100 files become 100 workspaces instead of meaningful groupings.

nodes.label: Membership Partition
nodes.description: Current hard partition prevents artifacts from participating in multiple bodies of work.

nodes.label: Significance Test
nodes.description: Groups that fail significance test are refused into dead end, contradicting requirement to never discard relevant context.

nodes.label: Resume Point Exclusivity
nodes.description: Resume point requires exclusive member and exclusivity requires recurrence, preventing single-sitting work restoration.

nodes.label: Formation Fixes
nodes.description: Formation has been largely fixed, reducing workspaces from 490 to 9 on real corpus.

nodes.label: Importance Failure
nodes.description: Importance calculation has not been fixed - still fails to properly identify significant work.

nodes.label: Behavioral Audit
nodes.description: Comprehensive backend audit examining system behavior against authority documents and real corpus.

nodes.label: Window Focus Failure
nodes.description: Window-title artifacts become permanently unavailable because system discards witnessed application identity.

nodes.label: Continue My Work
nodes.description: Canonical end-to-end behavior trace for work restoration - user asks to continue and immediately resumes without reconstruction.

nodes.label: Pipeline Trace
nodes.description: Complete pipeline trace from raw observation to Home presentation, identifying divergences from intended semantics.

nodes.label: Context Chain Empty
nodes.description: Context Chain and Blockers are empty by principled derivation - no canonical supporting relationship exists.

nodes.label: Execution Divergence
nodes.description: Interface announces one target but execution opens N targets - violates explainability requirements.

nodes.label: Human Thought Continuity
nodes.description: The founding premise of Evo: human thought is continuous but the digital world is not, forcing people to repeatedly reconstruct what they already knew.

nodes.label: Invisible Reconstruction Work
nodes.description: The unacknowledged cognitive cost of reconstructing context after interruption — the core problem Evo exists to eliminate.

nodes.label: Evo Mission Statement
nodes.description: Human thought should never have to begin twice — the permanent, unchanging purpose of Evo.

nodes.label: Epistemic Honesty
nodes.description: Evo accepts being incomplete but refuses to be dishonest; accepts being wrong but refuses to be untrustworthy.

nodes.label: System Adapts to Users
nodes.description: Evo will never ask users to adapt to the system; the system must adapt to them.

nodes.label: Success Measurement
nodes.description: Success is measured not by how much Evo knows but by how little users must remember.

nodes.label: Law I — Reality Precedes Interpretation
nodes.description: Evo only observes reality; all interpretation must originate from observable evidence and no interpretation may exist without supporting evidence.

nodes.label: Law II — Evidence Is Sacred
nodes.description: Observable evidence is the permanent, immutable foundation — it is never rewritten or discarded, and every higher-level structure must remain derivable from preserved evidence.

nodes.label: Law III — Interpretation Is Disposable
nodes.description: Every interpretation (workspaces, attachments, knowledge, restore plans) is provisional and replaceable; improving interpretation must never require rewriting evidence.

nodes.label: Law IV — Observation And Interpretation Must Never Be Confused
nodes.description: Observation records what happened; interpretation explains meaning. No interpreted state may masquerade as observed fact.

nodes.label: Law V — Preserve Uncertainty
nodes.description: When evidence does not justify certainty, the architecture must preserve ambiguity; uncertainty is legitimate system state, not failure.

nodes.label: Law VI — Under-Interpretation Is Better Than Over-Interpretation
nodes.description: Incomplete interpretation is recoverable; incorrect interpretation damages trust. Silence is preferable to fabrication.

nodes.label: Law VII — Replay Must Always Be Possible
nodes.description: Because evidence is immutable and interpretation disposable, the complete interpretation layer must always be reproducible by replaying evidence through improved interpretation.

nodes.label: Law VIII — History Must Never Change
nodes.description: Historical facts remain historical; snapshots are immutable records. Replay may improve future interpretation but must never rewrite history.

nodes.label: Law IX — The User Owns Judgment
nodes.description: Architectural decisions must preserve the user's authority over meaning, priorities, goals, and decisions. Evo assists; it never decides on behalf of the user.

nodes.label: Law X — Minimize Reconstruction, Never Thinking
nodes.description: Evo eliminates unnecessary re-thinking, not thinking itself. Novel reasoning belongs to the user; repeated reconstruction belongs to Evo.

nodes.label: Law XI — Every Decision Must Be Explainable
nodes.description: Every interpretation must remain attributable to observable evidence. Explanation is a first-class architectural requirement, not a debugging feature.

nodes.label: Law XII — Preserve Layer Separation
nodes.description: Each architectural layer has a single responsibility: observation captures reality, interpretation constructs meaning, retrieval locates information, restoration rebuilds capability, learning improves future interpretation.

nodes.label: Law XIII — Architecture Must Remain Local-First
nodes.description: All decisions must preserve local ownership of data; the architecture must never require cloud, remote computation, or external identity to function correctly.

nodes.label: Law XIV — Capability Is The Objective
nodes.description: Restoration's purpose is not perfect recall but restoring the user's capability to continue meaningful activity.

nodes.label: Law XV — Simplicity Is A Constraint
nodes.description: The architecture must contain the smallest set of concepts necessary; no abstraction may exist without irreducible responsibility; simpler models are preferred.

nodes.label: Law XVI — Identity Law
nodes.description: Only concepts requiring stable identity across time may exist as computational objects; descriptive concepts must be represented as relationships or derived values, not objects.

nodes.label: Law XVII — Epistemic Separation
nodes.description: A strict separation must be preserved between witnessed and inferred information; inferred information must never overwrite observed information.

nodes.label: Architectural Laws
nodes.description: The frozen set of 17 permanent constraints that define the boundaries architecture must never violate, independent of language, frameworks, or models.

nodes.label: Engagement
nodes.description: The fundamental unit of human activity in Evo's cognitive model; some engagements close naturally, others remain open across interruption enabling continuity.

nodes.label: Open Engagement Continuity
nodes.description: Open engagements make continuity possible; they are the cognitive foundation for work resumption in Evo.

nodes.label: Inferred Engagement from Evidence
nodes.description: Observers cannot directly perceive engagement; they infer it from observable evidence. This principle underpins Evo's evidence-based architecture.

nodes.label: Resumption Goal
nodes.description: Resumption succeeds when a person regains the ability to naturally continue meaningful activity; assistance should restore capability, not reproduce history.

nodes.label: Cognitive Model
nodes.description: Frozen v1.0 document defining the minimal cognitive assumptions required to understand why interrupted activity can later continue naturally.

nodes.label: Workspace Origination
nodes.description: The question of when something becomes actual work worthy of a Workspace; the proposal was superseded by RFC-0014 (Engagement Contract).

nodes.label: Prior Witness Floor Flaw
nodes.description: The root-cause finding: the D1 floor using prior_witness conflates Artifact history with Workspace legitimacy, causing the 100-workspaces Case D failure.

nodes.label: Declaration as Origination Authority
nodes.description: The proposed remedy: WorkDesignated/WorkGrouped/ContinuationSurface declarations and witnessed repository membership are the only two evidence classes that can honestly establish a body of work.

nodes.label: RFC-0014 Engagement Contract
nodes.description: The adopted successor to ARCH-PROP-0001 that defines the Engagement Contract and supersedes the rejected workspace origination proposal.

nodes.label: Single Fact Rule
nodes.description: Each level of the product states one fact, in one voice, on one surface, and defers everything else — the load-bearing design rule of UI-IA-0002.

nodes.label: Recognition Not Reconstruction
nodes.description: The UI's primary job is to make a person recognise where they were and press one thing; a screen that must be read has already failed.

nodes.label: Material Hierarchy
nodes.description: Six semantic surfaces differentiated by material (M0 environment, M1 recessed, M2 raised, search well, action surface, modal sheet) rather than by label.

nodes.label: Merged Continuation Control
nodes.description: The proposed arity-dispatched commit that merges Designation and Continuation Surface into one control; the load-bearing mechanism of UI-IA-0002.

nodes.label: Home Hero Surface
nodes.description: A single raised surface on Home that emphasises the globally designated workspace, making the dominant fact visually primary.

nodes.label: Partial Restoration as Normal Case
nodes.description: Partial restoration is the default presentation; there is no failure screen — a Continue where nothing opened shows the same layout reporting honest failures.

nodes.label: Current UI Defect Register
nodes.description: The comprehensive review of evo-desktop identifying defects D-01 through D-38, backend bugs BE-01 through BE-03, and the root cause of the SaaS-dashboard feel.

nodes.label: Simultaneity Failure
nodes.description: The central UI failure: fifteen informational blocks presented at once, at comparable weight, on identical surfaces, so nothing can be recognised and everything must be read.

nodes.label: BE-01: Surface Erasure Bug
nodes.description: handle_designation does not read the current continuation surface before deriving, so the derived surface depends on which handler last fired rather than on the canonical log — gates Phase 2.

nodes.label: B-02: State Signature Execution Report Erasure
nodes.description: state_signature keyed to (workspace_id, snapshots.len()) causes the execution report to erase itself when a successful restoration produces new Observations.

nodes.label: Evo Copy Voice
nodes.description: The product copy expressing epistemic humility without sounding apologetic — identified as the best part of the product and a moat.

nodes.label: app.rs Refactor
nodes.description: The desktop shell was rebuilt from a 2726-line monolithic app.rs into 583 lines of state/dispatch plus a visual foundation (theme.rs, ui.rs) and three screen modules.

nodes.label: Six Semantic Surfaces
nodes.description: The implemented material hierarchy: environment (banded vertical field), raised surface, recessed contextual plane (darker than environment), search well, lifted action surface, and modal sheet.

nodes.label: Eight-Role Typography Ramp
nodes.description: A fixed eight-role type ramp where each role fixes size, weight, tracking, and leading together; size-specific tracking (Display −0.6, eyebrow +0.9) and inverse leading.

nodes.label: audit_desktop_calls.py
nodes.description: A Python audit tool performing three compiler-like passes across ten desktop modules: call-site resolution, constant/variant/field resolution, and test-block name resolution.

nodes.label: 75 Unexecuted Unit Tests
nodes.description: 75 unit tests asserting semantic and perceptual invariants (recessed darker than environment, size-specific tracking, etc.) that are written but unexecuted due to environment constraints.

nodes.label: Arity-Dispatch Rejection
nodes.description: The merged continuation control (§3 of UI-IA-0002) was rejected: the proof obligation fails due to mutual non-implication of designation and continuation surface, no-revoke constraint, and deferred contract mapping.

nodes.label: Phase 0 Six Correctness Bugs
nodes.description: Five UI defects and one backend defect (BE-01) identified as real and requiring immediate fix regardless of design direction.

nodes.label: Safe IA Core
nodes.description: Most of UI-IA-0002's information architecture is validated as safe; only the arity-dispatched commit and BE-01 dependency were rejected.

nodes.label: RFC-0006 UI Boundary
nodes.description: RFC-0006 Requirements 1–7 are behavioural and binding on any UI surface; the interface has design freedom but is bounded by these and by the prohibition on presenting unestablished relations.

nodes.label: Observation Model v1.0
nodes.description: Defines the fundamental unit of evidence in Evo. Observation is the sole architectural foundation of cognition — Evo reasons only about evidence acquired from reality through Observation.

nodes.label: Engineering Principles
nodes.description: Core engineering principles guiding all Evo implementations. Empty file — principles captured in IMPLEMENTATION_PLAYBOOK.

nodes.label: Glossary
nodes.description: Canonical definitions of domain terms used across Evo. Currently empty.

nodes.label: Implementation Playbook
nodes.description: Defines how every implementation for Evo must be written. Architecture takes precedence; if implementation contradicts architecture, stop and explain instead of inventing a solution.

nodes.label: IS-0001 Observation
nodes.description: Sole architectural entry point transforming Candidate Observations into Canonical Observations via validation, canonicalization, identity assignment, integrity verification, provenance preservation, and durable persistence.

nodes.label: IS-0002 Observation Language
nodes.description: Canonical language for representing human work. Ensures every downstream layer interprets observational information using the same concepts regardless of OS, implementation, or collection mechanism.

nodes.label: IS-0003 Observation Schemas
nodes.description: Canonical structure definitions for each Observation type. Composes the Observation Language into concrete definitions and provides stable structural contracts between Collectors and Consumers.

nodes.label: IS-0004 Artifact Model
nodes.description: Canonical computational representation of an Artifact — the first computational object derived from canonical Observations representing Evo's current identity hypothesis about one external entity.

nodes.label: IS-0005 Artifact Acceptance
nodes.description: Defines the canonical process by which a Candidate Artifact becomes a canonical Artifact, establishing the boundary between transient identity derivation and persistent computational identity.

nodes.label: IS-0006 Identity Hypothesis
nodes.description: Transient computational belief that one or more canonical Observations describe the same Artifact. Exclusively owned and destroyed by the Artifact Engine after Acceptance; never persisted.

nodes.label: IS-0007 Artifact Identity Lifecycle
nodes.description: Complete lifecycle of Artifact Identity after acceptance: creation, revision, supersession, merge, split, retirement, and replay while preserving Evidence Is Sacred and Epistemic Separation principles.

nodes.label: IS-0008 Artifact Replay
nodes.description: Replay mechanism for reconstructing Artifacts from canonical Observations.

nodes.label: IS-0009 Artifact Engine
nodes.description: Engine responsible for Artifact construction, Identity Hypothesis creation, and Artifact Acceptance. Exclusively owns Identity Hypotheses.

nodes.label: IS-0010 Identity Derivation Contract
nodes.description: Contract governing the rules and guarantees for artifact identity derivation.

nodes.label: IS-0011 Workspace Model
nodes.description: Model that relates Evidence into cohesive Workspaces grouping related Artifacts and Observations.

nodes.label: IS-0012 Workspace Formation
nodes.description: Process of forming Workspaces from Observations and Artifacts.

nodes.label: IS-0013 Workspace Replay
nodes.description: Replay mechanism for reconstructing Workspaces.

nodes.label: IS-0014 Confidence Score
nodes.description: Defines the Confidence Score used to evaluate the strength of identity hypotheses and workspace formation decisions.

nodes.label: Observation
nodes.description: Fundamental unit of evidence in Evo. Records witnessed reality. Immutable once accepted. The sole admissible source of evidence.

nodes.label: Candidate Observation
nodes.description: Unvalidated input submitted to the Observation module for acceptance processing.

nodes.label: Canonical Observation
nodes.description: A validated, canonicalized, identity-assigned, integrity-verified Observation that has been durably persisted.

nodes.label: Artifact
nodes.description: First computational object derived from canonical Observations. Represents Evo's current identity hypothesis about one external entity.

nodes.label: Candidate Artifact
nodes.description: Transient pre-acceptance artifact created by the Artifact Engine before identity is confirmed and persisted.

nodes.label: Workspace
nodes.description: A cohesive group of related Artifacts and Observations. Workspaces relate Evidence.

nodes.label: Collector
nodes.description: Component that translates platform-specific observations into canonical Observation Language concepts before acceptance.

nodes.label: Consumer
nodes.description: Downstream component that depends exclusively on canonical Observation Language concepts.

nodes.label: Authority Order
nodes.description: Precedence hierarchy: Architecture > RFC > IS > Implementation. Implementation never overrides architecture.

nodes.label: Law: Evidence Is Sacred
nodes.description: Historical evidence (Observations) never changes. Interpretation is mutable; evidence is not.

nodes.label: Law: Epistemic Separation
nodes.description: Every conclusion requires evidence. Evidence never requires conclusions. Observation preserves; it never understands.

nodes.label: Law: Replayability
nodes.description: Schemas evolve but historical evidence does not. Any derived state can be replayed from Observations.

nodes.label: Schema Identifier
nodes.description: Immutable identifier assigned to each Observation Schema. Every Observation Schema possesses exactly one Schema Identifier.

nodes.label: Schema Version
nodes.description: Version assigned to each Observation Schema enabling evolution while maintaining backward compatibility.

nodes.label: Continuation Surface Declaration
nodes.description: A declared set of continuation subjects that remains ground truth and outranks every inference at Layer 3.

nodes.label: Continuation Subject
nodes.description: Individual subjects that compose a continuation surface, ordered canonically in ascending order.

nodes.label: Engagement Derivation
nodes.description: Process that determines what belongs to the same body of work through Requirements 1-7.

nodes.label: Affinity Bridging
nodes.description: Mechanism that dilutes specificity and blocks pipeline functionality.

nodes.label: Work Designation
nodes.description: Canonical evidence class that is both witnessed and discriminating, supplied by the person whose work it is.

nodes.label: Repository Membership
nodes.description: Distinguished relational signal of work continuity that was found to prevent the product from working.

nodes.label: Behavioral Contract
nodes.description: Permanent specification that defines observable behavior independently of implementation.

nodes.label: OpenAI Computer History
nodes.description: Feature launched August 13, 2026 that tracks Mac activity across apps and websites using Accessibility API.

nodes.label: Microsoft Recall
nodes.description: Local screenshot-based timeline system redesigned with encryption and Windows Hello auth after privacy backlash.

nodes.label: Rewind AI
nodes.description: Mac app that was killed by switch on Dec 19, 2025 after company pivoted to hardware and was acquired by Meta.

nodes.label: Category Creation
nodes.description: Process requiring teaching market problem exists, convincing buyers problem deserves budget, and establishing comparison framework.

nodes.label: We Don't Sell Saddles Here
nodes.description: Slack's foundational memo from July 31, 2013 about selling the ability to ride a horse better, not saddles.

nodes.label: Screen Recording Permission
nodes.description: macOS permission that creates significant user friction with no programmatic workaround.

nodes.label: GDPR Controller Status
nodes.description: Legal status where local-only processing likely still makes you a controller under Article 4(7).

nodes.label: Momentum Pitch Deck
nodes.description: The only A-grade artifact that meets verification standards with split problem/solution/product across multiple slides.

nodes.label: Raycast Waitlist Strategy
nodes.description: Strategy that grew from 130 DAU to 11,000 DAU in 12 months using waitlist momentum and long free runway.

nodes.label: Obsidian Community Strategy
nodes.description: Community-led growth reaching 1.5M+ MAU in 2026 with $0 raised and open plugin API.

nodes.label: Attention Engineering
nodes.description: AI-powered desktop assistant by Gen Z founders Aidan Guo (19) and Julian Windeck (23) that raised $1.25M pre-seed.

nodes.label: Supermemory
nodes.description: Memory API for LLMs to retain context across sessions, raised $2.6-3M seed with 18K+ GitHub stars.

nodes.label: The Browser Company Acquisition
nodes.description: Atlassian acquisition for $610M cash in October 2025, representing category-defining outcome for this space.

nodes.label: Local-First Monetization
nodes.description: Challenge where no purely-local, no-cloud Mac subscription exists in dataset; all monetize via cloud add-ons.

nodes.label: Local-First Investment Gap
nodes.description: No named investor has verified investment in local-first, on-device-AI, or AI-memory company in last 24 months.

nodes.label: Permission Drop-Off Data Gap
nodes.description: Genuine evidence gap where no published A/B test data or funnel analytics exist for permission prompts.

nodes.label: 23-Minute Fabrication
nodes.description: Popular statistic that could not be found in any Gloria Mark paper and appears to be fabricated.

nodes.label: Interruption Benefits
nodes.description: CHI 2008 finding that interrupted tasks were completed faster with no error increase, contradicting productivity loss narrative.

nodes.label: Prosumer Acquisition Difficulty
nodes.description: Point Nine Capital's assessment that scaling prosumer acquisition is insanely hard with high churn and low expansion.

nodes.label: Mac Utility Monetization Failure
nodes.description: Historical pattern where Mac utilities that reached scale did so for free, making monetization extremely difficult.
